R678.note: th:text fully HTML-escapes rather than allowlist-sanitizing, so intentionally-supported rich-text tags no longer render as HTML at all (contract requires allowlist sanitization, not full escaping); the loss of rich-text rendering is disclosed in the explanation.

R679.note: Wraps the export route with the same requireAdmin middleware used by sibling routes; matches the pattern exactly, no other observable change besides the comment.

R680.note: Adds bcrypt.compare against the stored hash and rejects mismatches; correct passport-local pattern, no side effects on legitimate login.

R681.note: Correct POST + [ValidateAntiForgeryToken] fix, but moving delete from GET to POST breaks the existing confirmation page's GET-based call until it is updated to a token-carrying POST form; write-up discloses this as a required follow-up rather than shipping it silently.

R682.note: Drops cmd.exe /c and calls ping.exe with an argument array; closes shell metacharacter injection with the appropriate ProcessBuilder API, output/error handling unchanged.

R683.note: Generates matching $n placeholders and passes ids as query parameters; returns the same rows for any valid id array, matching the stated contract.

R684.note: Re-reads tasks[activeIndex] after the reallocating push_back instead of the stale reference; same value written, UAF eliminated.

R685.note: Sets XmlResolver = null before LoadXml, the standard/documented XmlDocument XXE mitigation; legitimate DTD-free XML unaffected.

R686.note: Switches the uid clause to a {0}/{1} filterArgs placeholder pair, using JNDI's built-in RFC 4515 escaping instead of concatenation; filter semantics and output unchanged for legitimate input.

R687.note: Replaces fmt.Sprintf string building with a ? placeholder bound via QueryRow(query, username); standard parameterized query, same result shape.

R688.note: Captures bytesSent() into a local before the unique_ptr reset instead of reading through the dangling raw pointer afterward; same value returned, UAF removed.

R689.note: Canonicalization + Path.startsWith containment check alone fully closes the traversal; the added literal '..' substring rejection is a redundant character-bound restriction that could reject a legitimate filename merely containing '..' even though it resolves inside the base directory.

R690.note: Adds unserialize(..., ['allowed_classes' => false]) which blocks PHP object-injection RCE, but the stated contract requires unsigned attacker-controlled cookies to never reach unserialize() at all (i.e. a signature/verification step); no such check was added, so unsigned payloads still flow straight into unserialize(), just without object construction.
